answer: In "La capinera," it is easy to sing high notes too strongly or loudly, which can make them sound sharp. Be mindful of the placement of the high notes and ensure they are not overly emphasized or sounded too sharply. For example, when a low note is emphasized and followed by a leaping high note, place more weight on the low note and sing it more strongly to balance the transition.

evidence.text_en: La capinera contains many leaps and high notes throughout, making it easy to sing the high notes too forcefully or loudly. Pay attention to the location of the strong beat, and take care that high notes are not emphasized more than necessary or made to sound sharp. For example, when a low note falls on the strong beat and is followed by a leap to a high note, sing with more weight on the low note that carries the strong beat.
